title: Higher minimum salaries, expanded rosters among upcoming PWHL changes
summary: The Professional Women's Hockey League and its players association have agreed to a series of changes, including higher minimum salaries and expanded rosters.

image.caption: Ottawa Charge goaltender Gwyneth Philips (33) makes a save on Montreal Victoire's Catherine Dubois (28) and Jessica DiGirolamo (22) during first period PWHL playoff hockey action in Laval, Que., on Saturday, May 16, 2026. (Christopher Katsarov/Canadian Press/File)

blocks.text: The Professional Women's Hockey League and its players association have agreed to a series of changes, including higher minimum salaries and expanded rosters.
Training camps open on Nov. 18, with regular season starting Dec. 5
Minimum annual base salaries will rise to $52,500 US by the 2030-31 season from $42,000 this campaign.
Each team will carry 24 full active roster spots starting this season, up from 23.
Teams will not have reserve players this season after being allowed to carry three reserve contracts in previous campaigns.
One-game standard player agreements are being introduced to handle unexpected roster situations.
Training camps open Nov. 18, with the regular season beginning Dec. 5.
